title: Traced SDF AO: lower error after 16 accumulated frames, at no more field reads per pixel
additional_information:
Make the "Traced SDF (temporal)" ambient occlusion good sooner. The file to edit is accuracy/traced_ao.py: `trace(n, frame, noise, sample)` (one frame's visibility estimate per pixel) and `show(formula, traced, frames)` (what the screen shows). Its docstring states the interface and the rules, which the judge enforces before running it.

What it computes: per visible pixel of a 1280x720 render of a static scene (159 axis-aligned boxes: floor, two walls, stairs, shelves, crates), ambient visibility in [0, 1], compared with a ray-traced reference: 512 cosine-weighted rays per pixel, a hit counting as occluded within 1.12 m. Three camera views are judge cells and three more are held out; each view is scored at a fixed subset of 20,000 pixels.

How the judge runs it: it simulates the viewer on a still camera for 64 frames. Each frame trace() returns an estimate, the viewer accumulates it (mean += (est - mean) / frames, frames = min(frame + 1, 128); that rule is fixed), and show() turns the formula's AO, the mean and the frame count into what is displayed. `formula` is the shipped four-tap wall-correction AO (fixed, not editable). The score, err16, is the mean absolute error of the shown AO after 16 frames: how good the mode is a quarter of a second after a camera cut or a newly revealed surface. err1, err4 and err64 are reported too.

What trace() sees: the surface normal, the frame index, per-pixel noise in [0, 1) that changes every frame (interleaved gradient noise on the GPU), and sample(offset, live): the signed distance to the scene (half-float 128^3 volume over a 26 x 18 x 8 m box, voxels about 20 x 14 x 6 cm, clipped at +1.5 m, negative inside) at the pixel's surface point plus an offset, for the pixels where `live` is True. It does not see positions or the scene layout. The judge samples the field as the GPU does: 8-bit trilinear weights, half-precision result.

Cost: every live pixel in a sample() call is one 3D texture read in the shader, and the judge counts them. The seed uses about 14.0 reads per pixel per frame (2 directions, sphere-traced in up to 16 steps, most rays stopping early). Hard limit: 14.25 reads per pixel per frame, averaged over the 64 frames. Spending fewer reads where they matter less and more where they matter is fair.

The seed is what index.html ships: 2 cosine-weighted directions a frame (a Fibonacci pair rotated by the noise and offset per frame by golden-ratio sequences), each sphere-traced from 2 cm out to 1.12 m with steps of at least 6 cm, blocked where the field drops below min(0.025, 0.1 * t * (w.n)) (t*(w.n) is the distance to the pixel's own tangent plane, so its own surface never counts); show() blends formula and traced mean with traced weight frames / (frames + 8). Seed err16: 0.0267 on the judge cells, 0.0236 held out (formula alone: 0.0293 / 0.0266; after 64 frames 0.0234 / 0.0207).

Hard limits: at most 14.25 reads per pixel per frame; no worse than the seed after 1 frame (err1) or after 64 frames (err64) on any view, beyond 0.0005 / 0.0002. The held-out views must not get worse.

The winner is ported by hand to GLSL and checked on the GPU, where the AO is traced at half resolution and upsampled with depth- and normal-aware weights (which averages some noise the CPU model keeps). Keep trace() to what a fragment shader can do: fixed-length loops, arithmetic, no data structures.
ideas: Importance-sample directions: more directions toward the horizon or toward nearby geometry (a cheap probe tap or two), with the estimate reweighted so it stays unbiased
A soft visibility per direction from the closest approach along the ray (min of d / t, as in SDF soft shadows) instead of a hard hit, so each direction carries more information
Distance-dependent hit threshold or step schedule; stop rays early once they are clearly free
Better per-frame direction sets: stratification across frames (e.g. Hammersley / R2 sequences) so 16 frames cover the hemisphere evenly
Spend reads unevenly: 1 long ray plus several short contact rays, or more directions on frames 0-15 and fewer later
A control variate: trace the difference between true visibility and the formula's prediction, or weight show() by an estimate of the traced mean's variance instead of a fixed frames / (frames + 8)
